request.original_text: Create project: let coordinators download an event's sign-ups as a CSV.
request.restatement: Add a coordinator-only CSV download of an event's sign-ups to the volunteer portal, with docs, UAT, release and handoff.

clarifications.question: Which columns, in what order?
clarifications.answer: First name, Last name, Email, Shift, Signed up (UTC), ISO 8601 UTC.

clarifications.question: Who may export which events?
clarifications.answer: Any coordinator, any event, as for the sign-ups page today.

clarifications.question: File format details?
clarifications.answer: UTF-8 with BOM, comma-separated, RFC 4180 quoting, formula prefix on =, +, -, @.

clarifications.question: Database changes or deletion enforcement?
clarifications.answer: No database change; handling guidance only.

clarifications.question: Does anything already exist that this builds on, or is it from scratch?
clarifications.answer: The portal app and the coordinator guide exist; nothing for export has been started.

in: Staging test, UAT, release, rollback, announcement and handoff

assumptions.text: Docs ship with each deploy because the app serves docs/user-guide at /help.

epic.title: CSV export of event sign-ups

instructions.purpose: Turn a list of sign-ups into a safe CSV file body, tested on its own before any route uses it.
prerequisites: P0-T02 is done.

steps.text: Run git checkout main, git pull, then git checkout -b feat/signups-csv-serializer.
Create src/lib/csv.ts exporting toSignupCsv(signups), which takes the Signup list returned by getSignups.
Write the header row First name,Last name,Email,Shift,Signed up (UTC) and one row per sign-up, with createdAt as ISO 8601 UTC.
Quote cells per RFC 4180, start the file with a UTF-8 byte-order mark, and prefix any cell starting with =, +, - or @ with an apostrophe.
Create tests/lib/csv.test.ts with cases for the header, quoting, the formula prefix, an empty list and the byte-order mark.
Run npm run lint and npm test until both pass.
Push the branch, open a pull request to main using the template's Summary, Testing and Jira sections, and put this task's Jira key in the title.
Paste the pull request link into a comment on this task.

acceptance_criteria: toSignupCsv returns the five columns in order with RFC 4180 quoting and the formula prefix.
New tests pass and the ci check is green.
No new dependency is added.
verify: The ci check on the pull request is green.
instructions.done_today: The pull request is open with green CI and review requested, linked on this task.

instructions.purpose: Coordinators need to download an event's sign-ups as a file. This task adds the server route that returns the CSV.
prerequisites: P1-T01 is merged, so toSignupCsv exists in src/lib/csv.ts.
Your local setup from P0-T02 works.

steps.text: Run git checkout main, git pull, then git checkout -b feat/signups-csv-endpoint.
Open src/routes/events.ts, find the signups route and read signupsPage: it calls getEvent(id) and returns notFound(res) when the result is null.
Below that line, add router.get('/events/:id/signups.csv', requireRole('coordinator'), signupsCsv).
Write signupsCsv next to signupsPage: call getEvent(id) and return notFound(res) if null; then call getSignups(id) and pass the result to toSignupCsv.
Set Content-Type to text/csv; charset=utf-8 and Content-Disposition to attachment with filename event-<id>-signups-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv, using today's UTC date.
Create tests/routes/events.signups-csv.test.ts, copying the setup lines and the loginAs import from tests/routes/events.signups.test.ts.

Add six tests: coordinator on event 1 gets 200, text/csv, the header row First name,Last name,Email,Shift,Signed up (UTC) and 3 data rows; event 2 returns only the header; event 999 returns 404; volunteer gets 403; signed-out is redirected to /login; the file name header matches the pattern.
Run npm run lint and npm test until both pass.

Run npm run db:up, npm run seed and npm run dev; sign in as the README's seeded coordinator, open http://localhost:3000/events/1/signups.csv, check the columns First name, Last name, Email, Shift, Signed up (UTC) in order with 3 rows, then delete the file.
Push the branch and open a pull request to main with the template's Summary, Testing and Jira sections; put this task's Jira key (like VOL-12) in the title.
Paste the pull request link into a comment on this task.

acceptance_criteria: The route returns the plan's five columns in order, for coordinators only.
Volunteers get 403, signed-out users go to /login, unknown events get 404.
Six new tests pass, the existing suite passes, and the ci check is green.
No new dependency is added.
verify: The ci check on the pull request is green, and the local check showed the right columns and row count.
instructions.done_today: The pull request is open with green CI and review requested, linked on this task. The merge is P1-T03's dependency.

changes_existing.why_needed: No route returns sign-ups as a file today; the sign-ups route only renders the page.

tasks.title: Rehearse the rollback on staging and post the runbook

instructions.purpose: Start the production deploy of the version that passed staging tests and UAT.
prerequisites: P2-T02 sign-off records the staging commit.
P2-T03 says main was redeployed to staging.
P2-T04 is merged.

steps.text: Run git checkout main, git pull, git fetch --tags.

Copy the tested commit SHA from P1-T05 and run git log --oneline <that SHA>..main. Only the release-notes merge should be listed; if anything else appears, do not tag: comment the list, set this task to Flagged, mention the Program Director, and stop.
Open the latest staging deploy run and copy the deployed SHA from its summary; it must equal git rev-parse main. If not, handle it as in step 2.
Work out the new version as in CONTRIBUTING.md (v2.13.0 becomes v2.14.0) and check CHANGELOG.md uses it; if not, handle it as in step 2.
Run git tag -a <new version> -m 'Sign-ups CSV export', then git push origin <new version>.
Open the Actions tab, find the deploy run for the tag, and confirm it waits for the production environment review.
Post the run link in the release channel and on this task, and mention the Portal Admin to review the deploy.

acceptance_criteria: The tag is on the tested commit plus the release-notes merge, and staging runs that same commit.
Or, if extra commits appeared, no tag was pushed and the task is blocked with the list in a comment.
A production deploy run for the tag is waiting for review, and its link is on this task.
verify: git ls-remote --tags origin <new version> returns the tag, and the run link opens the waiting run.
instructions.done_today: The tag is pushed and the run waits for the Portal Admin's approval, or the task is blocked with a comment explaining why.
